1) Bitcoin (BTC)
- What it is: First cryptocurrency (2009), created by Satoshi Nakamoto. Peer‑to‑peer digital cash / store of value.
- Tech: Proof‑of‑Work (SHA‑256), decentralized ledger (blockchain), fixed supply cap 21 million, periodic “halving” of mining rewards.
- Use cases: Value transfer, censorship‑resistant store of value, settlement layer for other systems, institutional treasury asset.
- How to hold: custodial exchanges, software wallets, hardware wallets (recommended for long‑term).
- Risks: high volatility, regulatory/tax issues, irreversible transactions, custody/phishing risks, potential forks/security incidents.

2) Binance Coin (BNB)
- What it is: Native token of the Binance ecosystem (Binance Exchange + BNB Chain). Launched in 2017 (initially ERC‑20), migrated to Binance Chain / BNB Chain.
- Tech & role: Used for trading fee discounts on Binance, gas fees on BNB Chain, token burns reduce supply; BNB Chain uses a consensus model (PoSA / validator set) that is more centralized than major public PoW/PoS chains.
- Use cases: transaction fees, DeFi, tokens/DEXs on BNB Chain, staking/validator economics in some setups.
- Risks: centralization and regulatory scrutiny of Binance, smart‑contract risks on BNB Chain, market volatility.

3) WhatsApp, Instagram, Google — crypto relevance (summary as of mid‑2024)
- WhatsApp: Primarily a messaging app; no widely deployed native crypto transfer feature. Meta previously explored payments and wallet concepts (Diem/Novi) but Diem/Novi were discontinued; WhatsApp supports traditional payments in some countries via local rails (not crypto).
- Instagram (Meta): Meta rolled out NFT/display and creator payment experiments on Instagram and Facebook (allowing users to display NFTs and integrate with wallets in some regions). Availability and features vary by region and may change.
- Google: No native cryptocurrency. Google Cloud offers services for blockchain analytics, node hosting and partnerships with crypto firms; Google BigQuery hosts public blockchain datasets for analysis. Google Play permits legitimate crypto wallet/exchange apps under policy rules; Google Ads has had evolving crypto advertising rules (strict/regionally restricted historically).

4) Practical steps / security (quick)
- Learn basics, understand taxes and regulation in your country.
- Use reputable exchanges or OTC desks to buy/sell.
- For significant holdings use a hardware wallet and keep seed phrase offline.
- Enable strong account security: unique passwords, 2FA (preferably authenticator app), watch for phishing.
- Verify smart contracts and dApps before connecting wallets; use small test amounts.
